title: Sell Mineral Rights in Citronelle, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Citronelle, AL | Mobile County Oil Field
metaDescription: Own mineral rights in Citronelle, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer tied directly to the historic Citronelle Field's production and lease record.
heroLead: Citronelle is the name on Alabama's most significant oil discovery, a field that once ranked as the largest producing onshore field east of the Mississippi River, and mineral ownership here carries more documented history than almost anywhere else in the state.
intro: Discovered in 1955, Citronelle Field tapped the Rodessa and Donovan sands at depths beyond 10,000 feet, kicking off a leasing and drilling rush that touched nearly every tract in and around the town. Decades later, after primary production declined, the field saw a second life through CO2 enhanced oil recovery, injecting carbon dioxide to push additional oil toward existing wellbores. Owners here are more likely than in almost any other Alabama town to have an actual royalty history, though the character of that history varies enormously from one tract to the next depending on where it sits relative to the field's productive core.

sections.heading: Two generations of production
paragraphs: Citronelle's original primary production phase ran for decades before naturally declining, and the field was later redeveloped for CO2 flooding, a process that reworks existing reservoirs rather than requiring new discovery. That means some tracts here have two distinct royalty histories to review, an original production run and a later secondary or tertiary recovery phase, each with its own decline pattern.

sections.heading: Where your tract sits matters enormously
paragraphs: Because Citronelle Field covers a defined structural area rather than the whole town uniformly, a parcel inside the field's mapped productive limits is valued very differently than one on the surrounding periphery that was leased during the boom years but never actually produced. We check Alabama Oil and Gas Board field records against your specific legal description before quoting.

sections.heading: What we review for a Citronelle interest
paragraphs: For a producing or previously producing tract, we look at the well's production history, whether it's part of an active CO2 flood unit, and how comparable interests within the field have recently traded. For peripheral acreage with lease history but no production, we build a range from comparable bonus and permit activity instead.

faqs.question: My family has an old royalty history from Citronelle Field but nothing recent. What happened?
faqs.answer: Many original Citronelle wells declined and were shut in or converted for CO2 flood operations over the decades. We check the current status of your specific well or unit before quoting.

faqs.question: What is CO2 flooding and does it change what my interest is worth?
faqs.answer: It's a recovery method that injects carbon dioxide into a depleted reservoir to push out additional oil, and it can extend a well's productive life well beyond its original decline curve. If your tract is part of an active flood unit, that generally supports a stronger range than a fully depleted well.

faqs.question: My land is near Citronelle but I don't think it's ever produced. Is it still worth anything?
faqs.answer: It can be, though the range for acreage outside the field's productive limits is built from lease and permit comparables rather than a production record. We check your specific legal description against the field's mapped boundary first.
